code:
layer = nn.Linear(in_features=10, out_features=20)

x = torch.randn(32, 10)
y = layer(x)              # shape (32, 20)

layer.weight.shape  # torch.Size([20, 10])
layer.bias.shape    # torch.Size([20])
caption: y = x @ weight.T + bias -- last dimension must match in_features.

code:
# No activation: collapses to one linear layer
nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 20), nn.Linear(20, 1))

# With activation: genuinely non-linear
nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 20), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(20, 1))
caption: Composing linear functions just gives you another linear function.

steps.label: ReLU -- default for hidden layers
steps.sub: max(0, x), cheap, avoids vanishing gradients

steps.label: Sigmoid / Tanh -- output layers
steps.sub: squash to (0,1) or (-1,1); saturate as hidden layers

code:
model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(10, 32), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(32, 16), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(16, 1),
)
y = model(torch.randn(4, 10))  # shape (4, 1)
caption: nn.Sequential feeds each layer's output into the next.
